thread:
incident-bot: :warning: P1 alert — spike in token generation latency observed in hosted-prod (us-west-2). Trigger: 5xx/latency SLO breach. Pages fired to on-call. TL;DR: 10ms->2.4s token latency on some backends, customer-facing timeouts for streaming requests.

liam.oncall: Acknowledged. I'm working with infra to isolate whether this is GPU pressure vs networking. Paging infra and runtime teams. @sam.ops can you pull latest pod metrics and kernel logs?

sam.ops: pulling metrics now. seeing CPU steal on a subset of nodes + elevated kernel softirq. also a bump in NFS retries to model shard. attaching quick grep of relevant logs:
```
May 14 12:03:21 gpu-node-3 kernel: softirq: 2723416 0 0 0 0
May 14 12:03:22 nfs-client: retry read 5 to 10.0.0.12
```

erin.prodcomm: I'm drafting a customer-facing advisory. Posting a first-pass below — please review for accuracy and tone. Looking for: affected scope, mitigation steps, ETA, and follow-up notices.

erin.prodcomm: ```
We are currently investigating increased text generation latency affecting hosted inference in the US-West region. Some streaming requests may time out or experience delayed tokens. Our engineering team is actively mitigating the issue; there is no evidence of data loss. We will post updates every 30 minutes and notify when normal performance is restored.
Impact: Customers with workloads routed to us-west may see slower response times; a subset of streaming calls may fail to complete.
Mitigation: Traffic routing and autoscale adjustments are in progress. If you run critical low-latency services, consider switching to the eu-west or us-east region temporarily.
ETA: Investigation ongoing. Next update in 30 minutes.
``` 

sam.ops: couple edits — say "subset of customers" instead of "customers" and add that we've rolled back a recent kernel patch on affected nodes. Also include a safe workaround: retry with a 5s token timeout.

erin.prodcomm: updated draft with your edits. New version below.

erin.prodcomm: ```
We are investigating increased generation latency affecting a subset of hosted inference customers routed to the US-West region. Some streaming requests may time out or experience delayed tokens. Our engineering team is actively mitigating the issue and has rolled back a recent kernel patch on impacted nodes; there is no evidence of data loss. We will post updates every 30 minutes and notify when normal performance is restored.
Impact: Affected customers may see slower response times; streaming calls can timeout.
Mitigation: We've rolled back a kernel patch on nodes showing high softirq and are rebalancing traffic away from impacted hosts. As a temporary workaround, please increase client-side token timeouts to 5s or route requests to eu-west/us-east.
ETA: Investigation ongoing. Next update in 30 minutes.
``` 

julia.cs: wording looks good. Can we add a short note about customer support contacts and a link to incident status page? Also add a line about refunds/credits policy if SLA breach confirmed.

erin.prodcomm: good call. Added link placeholder and support instructions. New snippet:

erin.prodcomm: ```
..support.. If you're impacted, contact support@redwood.ai with subject line "Latency incident - us-west". We will evaluate credits if SLA thresholds are breached. Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2070012345
``` 

kevin-prod: Please don't mention refunds/credits in the initial advisory — escalate that to legal/finance first. Suggest replacing with "We will assess customer impact and follow up with any credits if applicable." Also add which models are affected (we saw larger impact on longer-context models).

erin.prodcomm: updated again, removed explicit refunds wording, added model note and changed support line to canned routing. Draft below for sign-off:

erin.prodcomm: ```
We are investigating increased generation latency affecting a subset of hosted inference customers routed to the US-West region. Some streaming requests may time out or experience delayed tokens. Our engineering team is actively mitigating the issue and has rolled back a recent kernel patch on impacted nodes; there is no evidence of data loss. We will post updates every 30 minutes and notify when normal performance is restored.
Impact: Affected customers, particularly workloads using longer-context models (>8k tokens), may see slower response times or streaming timeouts.
Mitigation: We have rolled back a kernel patch on nodes showing high softirq, rebalancing traffic away from impacted hosts, and temporarily increasing autoscaler headroom. As a workaround, clients can increase token timeouts to ~5s or route requests to eu-west/us-east.
Support: If you're impacted, contact support@redwood.ai with subject "Latency incident - us-west". We will assess customer impact and follow up on credits if applicable. Status updates: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2070012345
ETA: Investigation ongoing. Next update in 30 minutes.
``` 

liam.oncall: +1 from me. I'm fine to publish the initial advisory. @ops-bot can you run the publish checklist? I'll watch for ops followups and escalate to SRE lead if we don't see improvement in 15m.

ops-bot: Publishing checklist run:
- [x] Legal/PR clearance: acked by kevin-prod
- [x] Support routing verified
- [x] Status URL created
- [ ] Canary publish in 1m

ops-bot: Canary publish completed; no errors reported. Public advisory posted to status page and linked in customer comms channel.

liam.oncall: Published. I'll capture customer-impact notes for post-incident review. Keep posting updates here every 30m or sooner if we have new mitigations/resolution.

erin.prodcomm: Thanks all. I'll push a short customer email template next and prep the resolved notice when we have confirmation of restored performance.

incident-bot: NOTE: remember to include a resolved summary with root cause, impact numbers (customers affected, error rates, duration), and remediation steps for the postmortem.
